source: Sources: MIT News (19 Nov 2026), ScienceDaily (24 Nov 2026)

scenes.vo: A black hole the size of an atom could hide inside a star. And blow it up from inside.
scenes.cap: An atom-sized black hole could hide inside a star

scenes.vo: This is a new theory from MIT, published in the Astrophysical Journal. Nobody has seen one yet.
scenes.cap: New MIT theory (Astrophysical Journal). Not observed yet.

scenes.vo: These would be primordial black holes, from the early universe. About a millionth of Earth's mass, squeezed to the size of an atom.
scenes.cap: Primordial black hole: about a millionth of Earth's mass

scenes.vo: If a star captures one, it sinks to the core and eats slowly. Over several million years, about one percent of the star.
scenes.cap: Over several million years, it eats about 1% of the star

scenes.vo: Then jets form. Within a few dozen seconds, the star explodes.
scenes.cap: Jets form. Within a few dozen seconds: the star explodes.

scenes.vo: The clue would be a flash of X rays and gamma rays, then ultraviolet, visible light and radio. The authors say other events can look similar, so it's a search, not proof.
scenes.cap: Predicted clue: X/gamma flash, then UV, optical, radio

scenes.vo: If telescopes catch that pattern, we may finally find the smallest black holes in the universe.
scenes.cap: Catch that pattern = maybe the smallest black holes ever
